prompt: `sweep.py` printed R$ 23,448 at a cut of 0.2 and R$ 9,088 at 0.5. How many reais does the default leave on the table over the six test months?

choices.text: `sweep.py` steps unevenly between cuts on the left side of the chart
choices.why: The steps are even; the figure uses every half-hundredth.

choices.text: Stayers outnumber leavers fifteen to one

choices.text: The model is overfitted at low cuts
choices.why: The model is the same at every cut; only the line moves.

choices.text: Leavers cost more than stayers to reach
choices.why: Every credit costs R$ 40, whoever gets it.

choices.text: 0.20 wins, because round numbers are easier to explain to the business

prompt: A model whose chances of 0.3 are followed by about 30% of those rows leaving is called ___.

choices.text: It cannot be known without refitting the model
choices.why: The order of the rows is all it needs, and it has not changed.

choices.text: Higher than 0.80, because the chances are now honest

AUC is not scaled with the chances.
Yes. Halving keeps the order, and AUC reads nothing else.
